title: Reversal of established cataract without removing the lens

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a treatment that reverses an established, vision-impairing cataract while retaining the person's natural lens. It would need to reduce existing cloudiness, restore useful vision and leave the lens clear and stable. The central challenge includes age-related nuclear cataract, which affects the lens nucleus. Preventing cataract formation or slowing its progression would be valuable, but would not demonstrate reversal of established disease.

Age-related cataract involves aggregation of crystallin proteins and other accumulated damage within the avascular lens. The therapeutic goal therefore extends beyond making isolated proteins more soluble: treatment must restore transparency in an intact lens and produce a meaningful improvement in vision. Cataract surgery already restores sight by removing the cloudy lens and replacing it with an intraocular lens; this innovation would establish a different capability, biological reversal while preserving the natural lens.

significance.text: Cataract is a leading cause of blindness worldwide, so a durable lens-preserving treatment could have substantial public-health importance. The WHO fact sheet retained in the supplied review, dated 10 February 2026, attributes distance vision impairment or blindness to cataract in 94 million people within the population whose impairment could have been prevented or remains unaddressed. This figure describes that burden of impairment, rather than total cataract prevalence. The same revision states that one in two people globally who need cataract surgery cannot access it.

The direct consequence of successful reversal would be the ability to treat qualifying cataracts without extracting the lens. Reducing dependence on operating rooms and cataract surgeons would be an additional, conditional benefit: it requires a delivery method that is safe and effective outside surgical facilities. The reported lanosterol-synthase mRNA approach uses intracameral injections, and its authors explicitly acknowledge that delivery still requires ophthalmic surgical skills. Lens preservation alone therefore does not establish independence from surgical systems.

Conditional synthesis: an affordable treatment suitable for broad clinical or self-administered use could expand access and reduce demand for cataract operations. Those possibilities depend separately on manufacturing, distribution, diagnosis, monitoring and durable efficacy. The capability would address lens opacity; it would not itself repair unrelated retinal, optic-nerve or brain disease, or repair complications in an eye whose natural lens has already been removed. Its revolutionary character would lie in adding biological reversal to the treatment options, while surgery remains an established effective treatment.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is durable reversal of established human age-related lens opacity, including nuclear cataract, with restoration of useful vision and acceptable safety. The supplied evidence does not demonstrate that combined clinical outcome. Failures of lanosterol in excised human cataractous nuclei, and failures of lanosterol and 25-hydroxycholesterol in human lens-protein solubility experiments, identify concrete obstacles to translation. They apply to the compounds, preparations and conditions tested; they do not prove that every future treatment must fail.

A central scientific barrier is translating an effect on protein aggregation or an experimentally induced opacity into repair of accumulated damage in an aged human lens. Solubilizing isolated proteins, reducing opacity in a young animal and restoring the optical function of an intact human cataractous nucleus are different achievements. The reported negative and positive experiments use different preparations and disease models, so their outcomes do not constitute a single irreconcilable efficacy conflict.

Engineering synthesis: an effective intervention must deliver sufficient therapeutic activity to the relevant lens region, restore transparency without compromising lens function or surrounding ocular tissues, and maintain the benefit after treatment ends. The avascular anatomy makes delivery a distinct design problem. The 2025 mRNA study illustrates a possible delivery route, but its intracameral injections leave unresolved whether comparable efficacy could be achieved through a less demanding method suitable for widespread use.

current_state.text: Shanmugam and colleagues, in the December 2015 Indian Journal of Ophthalmology, studied 40 excised human age-related cataractous nuclei. Twenty were assigned to 25 mM lanosterol and twenty to a control solution for six days. Lanosterol did not reverse nuclear opacity under those conditions. This was an experiment on removed nuclei, rather than treatment of intact eyes, and it measured opacity rather than recovery of patient vision.

Daszynski and colleagues, in Scientific Reports on 11 June 2019, reported that a subsequent 48-hour incubation with 15 mM lanosterol liposomes failed to reverse experimentally induced rat-lens opacities or prevent further progression to the nuclear stage. Their separate human lens-protein experiments found that neither lanosterol nor 25-hydroxycholesterol increased solubility under the tested conditions. The rat-lens reversal result concerned lanosterol; the negative findings for both compounds concerned the protein-solubility experiments. These results constrain particular therapeutic approaches without establishing universal resistance to pharmacological reversal.

Song and colleagues, in Nature Communications on 26 September 2025, reported reduced cataract severity after intracameral administration of lipid nanoparticles carrying lanosterol-synthase mRNA in young rats exposed to selenite or galactose. The timing matters: treatment in the selenite experiment began before cataract induction, whereas treatment in the galactose experiment began after opacity had developed. The galactose result therefore provides evidence of improvement in existing experimentally induced opacity, while the selenite result includes a preventive component. Neither experiment demonstrates reversal of established aged human nuclear cataract.

On 17 July 2026, Ophthalmology Times reported that Lexitas Pharma Services and Ocusun had announced first-patient enrollment in a randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled pilot study of the lanosterol-derived eye drop ZOC2017217, identified as NCT07395986. This supports reported trial initiation, rather than completed controlled efficacy. The article also mentions exploratory human findings and another candidate's phase 1/2 report, but their underlying clinical reports were not independently supplied in the reviewed evidence. Those mentions cannot establish durable reversal of human nuclear cataract.

The supplied evidence contains no demonstration of durable reversal of established human nuclear cataract with restored acuity and a stable natural lens. However, the supplied freshness-search record is empty, so it cannot establish that no completed controlled human efficacy results existed anywhere by 1 November 2026. The 2025 paper's description of the unmet therapeutic need is an account at its publication date, rather than an exhaustive determination of the field's later status.

The supplied review assessed full article text for the principal experimental studies, allowing the stated methods and reported outcomes to be distinguished. Figures were not visually inspected, and the 2025 study's reporting-summary artifact was unreadable in the available extraction. Consequently, these descriptions reflect the reported textual findings and do not imply an independent audit of images or reporting quality. These limitations leave aspects of assessment incomplete; they do not by themselves invalidate the reported results.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: a randomized, masked, controlled human trial enrolling people with established, vision-impairing age-related cataract, with a prespecified nuclear-cataract subgroup. It should demonstrate clinically meaningful reduction in lens opacity together with improved visual acuity, while retaining the natural lens. Eligibility, opacity measurements, visual outcomes and thresholds for success should be specified before results are known. These are proposed criteria for this innovation, rather than established consensus standards.
completion_criteria.label: Controlled trial demonstrates meaningful opacity reduction with improved visual acuity

completion_criteria.text: Proposed durability and safety requirements: the improvement should be sufficient to avoid surgery under prespecified clinical criteria and remain meaningful for a prespecified follow-up period after dosing stops. The study should assess ocular safety and whether the retained lens remains optically useful and stable. Neither a clearer appearance without useful vision nor short-lived improvement during dosing would establish the full capability. Follow-up duration, acuity thresholds and acceptable adverse-event rates remain to be defined.
completion_criteria.label: Safe, stable vision improvement persists after dosing and avoids surgery

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: independently reproduced controlled results should establish which cataract subtypes, severities and patient populations benefit, and under what delivery conditions. Prevention in acute animal models, isolated-protein solubilization and uncontrolled human case series would provide supporting evidence but would not independently meet the proposed clinical demonstration. Finite trials would establish efficacy across the populations and conditions studied, rather than effectiveness for every cataract. Any claim of treatment outside surgical facilities would additionally require evidence for safe delivery and monitoring in that setting.
completion_criteria.label: Independent controlled replication establishes benefiting populations and delivery conditions

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: OPH-04, “A manufactured cornea that clears vascularized stromal opacity,” shares the objective of restoring a transparent optical path. OPH-03 concerns opacity within the natural lens; OPH-04 concerns the cornea and a manufactured replacement or repair capability. Success in either optical tissue would not establish repair of the other.

Roster-based synthesis: OPH-02, “Biological reconstruction of foveal cones, RPE, and their blood supply,” OPH-07, “One programmable repair for many photoreceptor and RPE gene defects,” OPH-08, “Reperfusion of established retinal capillary dropout,” and OPH-11, “Prevention of progression from early or intermediate AMD to late AMD,” concern retinal tissues, their genetic defects, circulation or disease progression. They could complement cataract reversal in an eye with multiple causes of impaired vision. Clearing the lens would not reconstruct retinal cells, correct their gene defects, restore capillaries or prevent AMD progression.

Roster-based synthesis: OPH-01, “Retinotopic reconnection of retinal ganglion cell axons to brain targets,” and OPH-10, “Arrest of glaucomatous ganglion-cell death when pressure is not the lever,” concern preservation or restoration of the neural pathway carrying visual information. Cataract reversal would improve transmission of light through the lens but would not establish ganglion-cell survival or correctly mapped reconnection to the brain.

Roster-based synthesis: OPH-05, “Patterned vision from the brain when the eye cannot send signals,” addresses visual function through brain-directed intervention, while OPH-09, “Reopening of the human visual critical period,” concerns renewed visual-system plasticity. OPH-03 repairs an optical obstruction and depends on downstream visual function; it does not itself establish either brain-generated patterned vision or reopening of developmental plasticity.

Roster-based synthesis: OPH-06, “A closed-loop control that sets axial eye growth,” concerns control of eye length and refractive development. Its overlap with OPH-03 is the broad goal of improving the eye's optical performance. Controlling eye growth and reversing accumulated lens opacity remain separate biological and engineering capabilities.

change_log.change: Preserved OPH-03 and its title while defining the target as reversal of established vision-impairing cataract, including nuclear cataract, with retention of a useful natural lens.
change_log.reason: This retains the concept's identity and separates the missing capability from prevention, isolated biochemical effects and established lens-replacement surgery.

change_log.change: Corrected the 2015 experiment to 40 total nuclei, with 20 receiving 25 mM lanosterol and 20 receiving control solution for six days.
change_log.reason: The reviewed methods contradict the earlier implication that all 40 nuclei received lanosterol.

change_log.change: Separated the 2019 lanosterol rat-lens experiments from the human lens-protein experiments involving both lanosterol and 25-hydroxycholesterol, and retained the supported 15 mM and 48-hour details.
change_log.reason: The earlier account combined distinct experimental scopes and incorrectly extended the rat-lens result to both compounds.

change_log.change: Added intracameral delivery, young-animal scope and the different dosing timelines for the 2025 selenite and galactose experiments.
change_log.reason: Preventive dosing and treatment after opacity develops provide different evidence, and neither establishes reversal of aged human nuclear cataract.

change_log.change: Described the 2026 ZOC2017217 development as company-reported initiation of a controlled pilot and qualified the article's additional human-result mentions.
change_log.reason: The retained news report supports enrollment but does not substitute for independently supplied completed clinical results.

change_log.change: Replaced the unrestricted claim that no effective drug or completed controlled trial exists with a statement bounded to the supplied evidence.
change_log.reason: The empty freshness-search record cannot establish worldwide absence of further results through 1 November 2026.

change_log.change: Used the retained WHO page's 10 February 2026 date, clarified the scope of the 94-million estimate and replaced the unverified historical 17% quotation with its current one-in-two surgical-access statistic.
change_log.reason: The retained revision supports those statements and uses a different denominator from the unavailable 2023 attribution.

change_log.change: Made reduced dependence on surgical infrastructure conditional on delivery capability, affordability and access.
change_log.reason: Lens-preserving efficacy does not automatically establish nonsurgical delivery; the documented mRNA route still requires ophthalmic surgical skills.

change_log.change: Expanded proposed completion criteria to include prespecified nuclear-cataract analysis, meaningful visual benefit, surgical eligibility, durability, safety and independent reproducibility.
change_log.reason: These make the proposed demonstration assessable without presenting invented thresholds as established standards or implying universal efficacy.

change_log.change: Integrated evidence-access limitations and explained relationships to every other supplied roster entry.
change_log.reason: The record should preserve the limits of the reviewed evidence and distinguish complementary ophthalmic capabilities without merging concepts.

unresolved_issues: Whether additional completed controlled human efficacy results existed by 1 November 2026 remains unresolved because the supplied freshness-search record is empty.

The historical WHO statement attributed to 10 August 2023, including the 17% access figure and its denominator, cannot be verified from the retained 2026 revision. Its omission does not establish that the historical statement was false.

The underlying reports for exploratory human findings and the other candidate's phase 1/2 results mentioned in Ophthalmology Times were not independently supplied; their methods, outcomes and relevance to established nuclear cataract remain unresolved.

The optimal therapeutic mechanism and whether any approach can durably restore the optical function of an aged human cataractous nucleus remain unknown. Tested candidate failures do not resolve feasibility for all approaches.
Trial thresholds for meaningful opacity reduction, acuity improvement, avoidance of surgery, post-treatment follow-up and acceptable safety remain to be specified.
The cataract subtypes, severities and patient populations that might respond, and whether effective delivery can occur outside facilities requiring ophthalmic surgical skills, remain unresolved.

Figures were not visually inspected in the supplied review, and the 2025 reporting-summary artifact was unreadable in extraction; independent image and reporting-quality assessment remains incomplete.
No historical comparison examples were supplied to calibrate the scale of the innovation beyond its direct clinical and conditional access implications.

brief.title: Clearing cataracts while keeping the natural lens
possible: People whose sight has clouded because of a cataract could regain useful vision while keeping their natural lens. Treatment would clear existing cloudiness and leave the lens stable, including when age-related damage affects its centre.
why: Cataract is a leading cause of blindness. Reversing it would give people another way to recover sight alongside surgery, which replaces the cloudy lens. An affordable treatment suitable for use outside surgical facilities could also reach people who lack access to an operation.

sources.showed: WHO identifies cataract as a leading cause of sight loss and reports that half of people who need cataract surgery cannot access it.
sources.quote: The leading causes of vision impairment and blindness are refractive errors and cataracts.
sources.cited_for: Cataract causes widespread sight loss, and access to surgery remains limited.
sources.not_established: These population estimates do not establish that a treatment can reverse cataracts.

sources.showed: Lanosterol, a natural compound studied for clearing cataracts, failed to clear cloudiness in removed human lens centres with age-related cataract.
sources.quote: Lanosterol 25 mM solution did not reverse opacification of human age-related cataractous nuclei.
sources.cited_for: A direct test in human cataract tissue found no reversal with this preparation.
sources.not_established: The experiment tested removed tissue, rather than treatment of intact eyes or recovery of vision.

sources.showed: Lanosterol failed to clear experimentally clouded rat lenses. Separate tests found that it and a related compound did not make human lens proteins more soluble.
sources.quote: failed to either reverse these lens opacities or prevent the further progression of cataracts to the nuclear stage.
sources.cited_for: These tests found obstacles to clearing cataracts by dissolving clumped lens proteins.
sources.not_established: Failure under these conditions does not establish that all treatments must fail.

sources.showed: Injections into young rats' eyes delivered mRNA, instructions for making a protein that produces lanosterol. Cloudiness improved, including in an experiment where treatment began after cataracts developed.
sources.quote: ultimately increasing lens transparency in both cataract models.
sources.cited_for: An animal experiment showed improvement in existing, experimentally induced cloudiness.
sources.not_established: Young-rat results do not establish lasting reversal of age-related human cataract; the injections still require eye-surgery skills.

sources.showed: The companies announced that a controlled pilot trial of a lanosterol-derived eye drop had begun enrolling patients with age-related cataracts.
sources.cited_for: A candidate eye drop has reached controlled human testing.
sources.not_established: Starting a trial does not establish that the drops safely restore vision or keep the lens clear.

shown: Song and colleagues improved existing cloudiness in young rats with experimentally induced cataracts. Earlier lanosterol tests failed in removed human lens centres and rat lenses. A human eye-drop trial has begun, but lasting reversal of age-related human cataract with restored vision remains to be demonstrated.
missing: A controlled human trial must demonstrate clearer lenses and useful vision in established age-related cataract, including cloudiness at the lens centre.
Vision gains must last after treatment stops, safely keeping the natural lens useful and avoiding surgery.
Independent studies must establish who benefits and which delivery methods work.

milestones.label: A controlled human trial shows clearer lenses and better sight
milestones.explanation: A controlled trial would have to show meaningful clearing and sharper vision while retaining the lens, including in cataracts affecting its centre. This would establish reversal in people.

milestones.label: Safe vision gains last after treatment and avoid surgery
milestones.explanation: Improvement would have to persist after dosing stops, safely keeping the lens stable and avoiding surgery under predefined criteria. This would establish a lasting clinical benefit.

milestones.label: Independent trials establish who benefits and how treatment works
milestones.explanation: Independent controlled trials would have to reproduce benefits across defined cataract types and patient groups under specified delivery conditions. This would establish reproducibility and practical limits.

uncertain: Can any treatment repair enough accumulated damage in an aged human lens to restore lasting clarity and vision?
How much improvement, how long a benefit and what level of side effects would count as success?
Could an effective treatment be delivered and monitored safely outside facilities with eye-surgery expertise?

page.title: Pharmacological reversal of age-related cataract
page.definition: A drug treatment reduces an existing age-related cataract, a clouding of the eye’s natural lens, and improves the vision impaired by it while retaining the lens. Nuclear cataract affects the lens centre; cortical and posterior subcapsular cataracts affect outer fibres and the region beneath the rear capsule.

goal.need: Cataract accounts for an estimated 94 million cases of preventable or unaddressed distance vision impairment or blindness worldwide. Half of the people who need cataract surgery cannot access it. Surgery replaces the cloudy lens with an artificial one. A drug that restored vision while preserving the natural lens could help people who cannot obtain or undergo the operation. Its reach would depend on where patients could receive treatment and what they would have to pay.

completion.title: FDA approves a drug for reversing established age-related cataract while retaining the natural lens.
completion.criterion: FDA grants marketing approval for an indication covering reduction of established age-related lens opacity and improvement of the vision impaired by it, with the natural lens retained. The approved indication and supporting clinical evidence must cover the cataract subtype being counted. Approval solely for prevention, slower progression or postoperative treatment does not satisfy this indication. Efficacy, safety, dosing and follow-up are assessed within the approved product’s evidence and labeling; no universal numerical reversal threshold is asserted.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, general new-drug approval and labeling requirements described in Step 4: FDA Drug Review; applied here to a cataract-reversal indication.
completion.threshold_quote: In cases where FDA determines that a drug has been shown to be safe and effective for its intended use
completion.basis: Marketing approval supplies an external decision on efficacy, safety, labeling and manufacturing. These are general drug requirements, not a published cataract-specific definition of reversal. Nuclear, cortical and posterior subcapsular cataracts are distinguished by LOCS III and must be counted only within the studied indication. No common numerical opacity, acuity or post-treatment durability requirement was located.

milestones.title: A cataract drug shows pharmacological activity and is reasonably safe for initial human testing.
milestones.criterion: The candidate exhibits pharmacological activity that justifies further development, and the nonclinical pharmacology and toxicology data support a determination that the proposed initial exposure in humans is reasonably safe.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Drug Development and Review Definitions, Investigational New Drug Application section. This is a general candidate-development gate, not a cataract-specific animal efficacy cutoff.
milestones.threshold_quote: determine if the product is reasonably safe for initial use in humans, and if the compound exhibits pharmacological activity that justifies commercial development.

milestones.title: At least one person receives a cataract drug in a clinical investigation under an effective IND.
milestones.criterion: At least one participant receives the investigational cataract drug under an effective US investigational new drug application (IND). The IND takes effect 30 days after FDA receives it unless FDA places the investigation on clinical hold, or earlier if FDA notifies the sponsor that the investigation may begin. Enrollment alone does not establish dosing.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.40(b) and (d), governing initiation of human investigations.
milestones.threshold_quote: An investigator may not administer an investigational new drug to human subjects until the IND goes into effect under paragraph (b) of this section.

milestones.title: More C-KAD patients than placebo patients gain ≥0.30 logCS at ≥2 spatial frequencies by day 120.
milestones.criterion: Compare day-120 responder proportions by assigned treatment in the trial population with age-related, low-grade nuclear cataract. A responder gains at least two chart patches (0.30 log units of contrast sensitivity) from baseline under dim illumination at two or more of 1.5, 3, 6, 12 and 18 cycles per degree. The registered unit is the patient. An analysis limited to eyes selected after the trial cannot establish this patient-level comparison.
milestones.set_by: Livionex, C-KAD protocol CK-0103, retrospectively registered as NCT06365762. The registry specifies low-grade nuclear cataract and lists assessments at days 30, 60, 90 and 120.
milestones.threshold_quote: Proportion of patients with ≥ 2-patch (0.30 logCS) contrast sensitivity improvement in at least two spatial frequencies under mesopic illumination

milestones.title: Controlled clinical investigations establish the claimed lens-preserving cataract-reversal effect.
milestones.criterion: Adequate and well-controlled clinical investigations establish the claimed reversal effect in the specified cataract subtype and provide evidence for assessing safety and benefit–risk before marketing approval. The studies distinguish the drug effect from spontaneous change, placebo effects and biased observation. FDA evaluates the total evidence. Its June 2026 draft guidance discusses one adequate controlled investigation plus confirmatory evidence; that guidance is nonbinding and does not prescribe a cataract-specific effect size, sample size or follow-up duration.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 314.126; evidentiary approaches are also discussed in its June 2026 revised draft effectiveness guidance.
milestones.threshold_quote: provide the primary basis for determining whether there is “substantial evidence” to support the claims of effectiveness for new drugs.

milestones.title: An established lens opacity receives a lower grade after drug treatment in a laboratory model.
milestones.criterion: Grade photographs of the same cataractous lens or excised lens nucleus before and after drug exposure. Show a decrease from its pretreatment opacity grade and report the comparison with control tissue where a control is used. For a subtype-specific result, identify the affected region of the lens. A change in protein solubility alone does not measure lens opacity.
milestones.set_by: Paired photographic grading of established lens opacity, used by Zhao and colleagues in rabbit lenses, Shanmugam and colleagues in human lens nuclei, and in studies of age-related cataract in cynomolgus monkeys.
milestones.threshold_quote: Pre- and post-immersion photographs were graded by two masked observers and collated for the regression or progression of lens opacity.

milestones.title: FDA files a new drug application for reversal of established age-related cataract.
milestones.criterion: On the new drug application pathway, FDA files the application seeking a lens-preserving reversal indication and notifies the applicant. FDA ordinarily determines within 60 days of receipt whether the application is sufficiently complete for substantive review. Submission by the sponsor alone does not meet the filing milestone.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 314.101(a).
milestones.threshold_quote: Within 60 days after FDA receives an NDA, the Agency will determine whether the NDA may be filed.

not_found: Searches of FDA and EMA guidance, NEI research priorities, ophthalmology society guidance and cataract trial records found no common numerical definition of pharmacological cataract reversal or required post-treatment durability.
No pivotal controlled result establishing sustained lens-preserving reversal of established age-related cataract with improved vision was located.
Public FDA IND authorization documents and complete nonclinical safety packages for C-KAD and ZOC2017217 were not located.
ClinicalTrials.gov study pages did not render complete records; the C-KAD endpoint was accessible through a registry mirror.
No day-120 patient-level responder counts by randomized arm for the full C-KAD trial population were located in the registry or published reports.

results.finding: Lanosterol failed to reverse induced rat-lens opacities; 6 lenses per group.
results.detail: All treated lenses progressed to mature cataracts with nuclear involvement. The experiment did not establish pharmacological activity supporting development or nonclinical safety for initial human exposure.
results.quote: While transparency in the control lenses appeared to be minimally affected, lanosterol failed to reverse opacities or halt the progression of cataracts in all treated lenses.

results.finding: Lanosterol failed to reverse induced cortical opacity in rat lenses; 6 lenses per group.
results.detail: Ouabain induced cortical opacities before lanosterol exposure. The study did not establish pharmacological activity supporting development or nonclinical safety for initial human exposure.
results.quote: While transparency in the control lenses appeared to be minimally affected, lanosterol failed to reverse opacities or halt the progression of cataracts in all treated lenses.

results.finding: hLSS mRNA-LNPs reduced cataract development in a nuclear cataract model; 8 rats received treatment.
results.detail: Treatment began before selenite-induced cataract formation. The rat safety assessments do not establish reasonably safe initial human exposure.

results.finding: hLSS mRNA-LNPs reduced established cortical turbidity in 9 treated rat lenses over 8 days.

results.finding: In a phase 1/2 C-KAD trial, 21 treated eyes were included in the subgroup analysis.
results.detail: The reported human treatment bears on the milestone, but the source does not establish that dosing began under an effective IND.

results.finding: In 41 eyes, 66.7% of C-KAD-treated eyes met the contrast-sensitivity endpoint versus 35.0% on placebo.
results.detail: This controlled subgroup analysis reports improved visual function and a lens-density finding, but does not establish cataract reversal or provide sufficient safety and benefit–risk evidence for marketing approval.
results.quote: The primary endpoint of the proportion of eyes with mesopic CS improvements ≥ 0.30 logCS (equivalent to 100% CS improvement) in at least two of the five spatial frequencies was significantly greater for C-KAD (66.7% vs. 35.0% for placebo, P = .043) at Day 120.

results.finding: All 18 cataractous rat lenses progressed to apparent nuclear involvement after lanosterol exposure.

results.quote: In fact, lens opacities in all treated lenses exposed to lanosterol progressed to the more advanced mature cataract stage with apparent nuclear involvement.

results.finding: Six rat lenses with ouabain-induced cortical opacity showed no reversal after 48 hours of lanosterol exposure.

results.quote: While transparency in the control lenses appeared to be minimally affected, lanosterol failed to reverse opacities or halt the progression of cataracts in all treated lenses.

results.finding: In 18 cataractous rat lenses, lanosterol failed to halt progression to apparent nuclear involvement.
results.detail: Nuclear involvement was an endpoint of the induced rat model. The source did not test established age-related nuclear cataract in this assay.
results.quote: In fact, lens opacities in all treated lenses exposed to lanosterol progressed to the more advanced mature cataract stage with apparent nuclear involvement.

results.finding: Six rat lenses with induced cortical opacities showed no reversal at 15 mM lanosterol.
results.quote: While transparency in the control lenses appeared to be minimally affected, lanosterol failed to reverse opacities or halt the progression of cataracts in all treated lenses.

results.finding: In 8 rats with induced nuclear cataract, treated eyes had lower grades than untreated fellow eyes at age 25 days.
results.detail: The study graded cataracts by slit lamp at age 25 days and photographed excised lenses at age 27 days.
results.quote: A further analysis of the cataract stage confirmed that cataract development in the injected eye was significantly lower than the uninjected contralateral eye

results.finding: In 9 treated rat lenses with galactose-induced cortical cataract, turbidity area declined over 8 days.
results.detail: The analysis normalized turbidity area to the corresponding lens. It did not assign before-and-after opacity grades.
results.quote: Following administration of mLNPs, the relative turbidity area including annular equatorial-like vesicles and radial turbidity in the lenses diminished over time

results.finding: The candidate reduced nuclear cataract severity in 8 treated rats and showed tolerability in a separate 24-hour rat assessment.
results.detail: The safety cohort size is unspecified in the supplied text. The cataract experiment began dosing before selenite induction.
results.quote: Injection of the resulting hLSS mRNA-LNPs into the anterior chamber of eyes could effectively attenuate cataract severity without noticeable adverse effects in two rat cataract models mimicking age-related and diabetic cataracts.

results.finding: The candidate reduced cortical turbidity in 9 treated rat lenses and showed tolerability in a separate 24-hour rat assessment.
results.detail: The cortical model was galactose-induced. The safety cohort size is unspecified in the supplied text.
results.quote: Injection of the resulting hLSS mRNA-LNPs into the anterior chamber of eyes could effectively attenuate cataract severity without noticeable adverse effects in two rat cataract models mimicking age-related and diabetic cataracts.

results.finding: Among 40 excised human cataract nuclei, zero lanosterol-treated nuclei received a lower opacity grade from both observers.
results.detail: Lanosterol was only partially soluble in the test solution.
results.quote: One of the observers felt that one nucleus appeared less opaque, but this was not supported by the other observer and is too weak a link to rely upon

results.finding: In a 49-participant NAC trial, the 24-month comparison with controls included nuclear opacities (reported p < 0.001 across the listed opacity types).
results.detail: The abstract does not give the nuclear subgroup size, a nuclear-specific effect estimate, or separate nuclear opacity and visual outcomes.
results.quote: The overall clinical results observed in the NAC-treated group by the 24-month period of examination differed significantly (p < 0.001) from the control group in the eyes with cortical, posterior subcapsular, nuclear or combined lens opacities.

results.finding: In a 49-participant NAC trial, the 24-month comparison with controls included cortical opacities (reported p < 0.001 across the listed opacity types).
results.detail: The abstract does not give the cortical subgroup size, a cortical-specific effect estimate, or separate cortical opacity and visual outcomes.
results.quote: The overall clinical results observed in the NAC-treated group by the 24-month period of examination differed significantly (p < 0.001) from the control group in the eyes with cortical, posterior subcapsular, nuclear or combined lens opacities.

results.finding: In a 49-participant NAC trial, imaging showed fewer posterior subcapsular opacity areas. Overall, 41.5% of treated eyes improved on image analysis.
results.detail: The 41.5% figure applies to treated eyes overall. The abstract gives no posterior subcapsular subgroup size or visual outcome.
results.quote: Topographic studies indicated fewer areas of posterior subcapsular lens opacity and 41.5% of treated eyes had improvement in image analysis characteristics.

results.finding: After lanosterol, cortical opacity in 3 aged macaques (6 eyes) showed its greatest decrease from baseline at day 14.
results.detail: The reported P < 0.05 compares the day-14 and day-21 reductions. The supplied text gives no numerical grade change from baseline.
results.quote: After reaching the highest reduction rate of lens opacity at 14 days, the opacification recovered at 21 days.

results.finding: Nuclear opacity in 3 aged macaques (6 eyes) showed no significant change over 21 days after lanosterol.

results.finding: Across 6 lanosterol-treated macaques, including 3 with cortical cataract, mild conjunctival swelling resolved within 1 week.
results.detail: The ocular tolerability results were reported across the treated groups.
results.quote: Only mild conjunctival swelling was evident, which subsided within 1 week

results.finding: In 3 macaques with nuclear cataract, aqueous lanosterol reached 28.58 ng/mL after treatment.
results.detail: The concentration was measured on day 14. The ocular tolerability results were reported across both treated groups.
results.quote: At Day 14, the lanosterol in aqueous humor of the cortical and nuclear cataract groups significantly increased to 31.61 and 28.58 ng/ml compared to the 7 and 21 days

results.finding: The phase 1/2 treatment analysis included 21 eyes in the C-KAD arm.
results.detail: The sample size counts eyes. The Nuclear case assignment follows the C-KAD trial context in the milestone descriptions.
results.quote: Forty-one subject eyes were included in the subgroup analysis (C-KAD n = 21, placebo n = 20).

results.finding: Among 41 selected eyes, the day-120 contrast sensitivity responder rate was 31.7 percentage points higher with C-KAD.
results.detail: Eyes were selected for baseline mesopic scores of 1–7 patches at all five frequencies. The Nuclear case assignment follows the C-KAD trial context in m3.
results.quote: The primary endpoint of the proportion of eyes with mesopic CS improvements ≥ 0.30 logCS (equivalent to 100% CS improvement) in at least two of the five spatial frequencies was significantly greater for C-KAD (66.7% vs. 35.0% for placebo, P = .043) at Day 120.

results.finding: In the 41-eye randomized trial subgroup, mean mesopic AULCSF improved by 0.19 logCS more with C-KAD than placebo at day 120.
results.detail: Lens density was exploratory. The abstract gives no imaging subgroup size. The Nuclear case assignment follows the C-KAD trial context in the milestone descriptions.
results.quote: The mean change in AULCSF (mesopic) was significantly larger for C-KAD, with 0.25 logCS improvement, versus placebo with 0.06 logCS improvement (P = .020) at Day 120.

results.finding: In 3 cynomolgus monkeys with cortical cataract, the decrease in peripheral opacity grade after lanosterol peaked at day 14.
results.detail: The improvement was transient. The supplied text reports the direction and timing of the change and refers to a supplementary table for individual grades.
results.quote: In the lens of cortical cataract, the peripheral opacification decreased with time, especially during the first 2 weeks after lanosterol–thermogel injection

results.finding: In 3 cynomolgus monkeys with nuclear cataract, opacity grades showed no significant change over 21 days after lanosterol.
results.quote: In nuclear cataractous eyes, the reduction rate of lens opacity showed no significant changes during the 21-day follow-up

results.finding: Lanosterol reduced cortical opacity in 3 monkeys. Across all 6 treated monkeys, mild conjunctival swelling resolved within 1 week.
results.detail: Tolerability observations were reported for the treated cohort as a whole. The paper gives no proposed initial human exposure or toxicology assessment tied to it.
results.quote: Only mild conjunctival swelling was evident, which subsided within 1 week

results.finding: In 3 cynomolgus monkeys with nuclear cataract, aqueous lanosterol reached 28.58 ng/ml after subconjunctival dosing.
results.detail: The concentration peaked at day 14. Ocular tolerability was reported across both treated subtypes, and the paper provides no toxicology assessment tied to a proposed initial human exposure.

results.finding: Among 10 selenite-exposed Wistar rat pups given NACA eye drops, 3 fewer had grade 2 nuclear opacity after treatment.
results.detail: The treated pups also received NACA injections before baseline. The eye drops ran from postpartum day 15 through day 30.
results.quote: However, treatment with NACA eye drops decreased the severity of cataract formation, where five rats out of the ten (50%) had grade 2 cataracts, four rats had grade 1 cataracts, and one rat had no cataract (grade 0).

goal.need = "Cataract accounts for an estimated 94 million cases of preventable or unaddressed distance vision impairment or blindness worldwide. Half of the people who need cataract surgery cannot access it. Surgery replaces the cloudy lens with an artificial one. A drug that restored vision while preserving the natural lens could help people who cannot obtain or undergo the operation. Its reach would depend on where patients could receive treatment and what they would have to pay.". Reason: The current rationale gives the access figures but leaves the practical benefit of keeping the lens unexplained.

add statement by US National Institutes of Health, Small Business Innovation Research programme, 2016: "a safe effective topical treatment for the reversal of cataracts". Reason: The NIH award documents a funded project whose stated objective was topical cataract reversal.

add milestone after None: "An established lens opacity receives a lower grade after drug treatment in a laboratory model.". Reason: The existing sequence starts with readiness for human exposure and omits the earlier experiment that directly tests whether established lens opacity can regress.

edit m1: criterion = "The candidate exhibits pharmacological activity that justifies further development, and the nonclinical pharmacology and toxicology data support a determination that the proposed initial exposure in humans is reasonably safe."; refs = [4]. Reason: The criterion mixes individual lens experiments with the separate FDA question of whether the evidence supports initial human exposure.

edit m2: criterion = "At least one participant receives the investigational cataract drug under an effective US investigational new drug application (IND). The IND takes effect 30 days after FDA receives it unless FDA places the investigation on clinical hold, or earlier if FDA notifies the sponsor that the investigation may begin. Enrollment alone does not establish dosing."; refs = [9]. Reason: Trial enrollment and planned sample sizes obscure the two facts needed to meet this milestone: an effective IND and actual dosing.

edit m3: title = "More C-KAD patients than placebo patients gain \u22650.30 logCS at \u22652 spatial frequencies by day 120."; criterion = "Compare day-120 responder proportions by assigned treatment in the trial population with age-related, low-grade nuclear cataract. A responder gains at least two chart patches (0.30 log units of contrast sensitivity) from baseline under dim illumination at two or more of 1.5, 3, 6, 12 and 18 cycles per degree. The registered unit is the patient. An analysis limited to eyes selected after the trial cannot establish this patient-level comparison."; set_by = "Livionex, C-KAD protocol CK-0103, retrospectively registered as NCT06365762. The registry specifies low-grade nuclear cataract and lists assessments at days 30, 60, 90 and 120."; set_by_kind = "protocol"; threshold_quote = "Proportion of patients with \u2265 2-patch (0.30 logCS) contrast sensitivity improvement in at least two spatial frequencies under mesopic illumination"; threshold_ref = 10; refs = [10, 13, 14, 24]. Reason: The registry counts patients with low-grade nuclear cataract, while the positive post hoc analysis counted selected eyes and cannot establish the registered patient-level result.

add milestone after m4: "FDA files a new drug application for reversal of established age-related cataract.". Reason: FDA’s acceptance of a new drug application for substantive review is a verifiable step between clinical evidence and the approval decision.
remove not found 3. Reason: The AAO’s December 2024 summary is available and explicitly distinguishes the initial trial from the post hoc analysis.

add not found: "No day-120 patient-level responder counts by randomized arm for the full C-KAD trial population were located in the registry or published reports.". Reason: The missing counts are needed to judge the registered C-KAD responder endpoint.
remove statement 0. Reason: WHO’s statement identifies cataract as a cause of vision loss without naming pharmacological reversal as a goal.
